paper.title: Efficient Explorative Key-term Selection Strategies for Conversational Contextual Bandits

unmapped: Conversational feedback: in addition to arm feedback, the learner may query up to floor(b(t)-b(t-1)) key-terms per round (b(t)=b*t) and observes noisy linear feedback x_tilde_k^T theta* + 1-sub-Gaussian noise for each queried key-term
The key-term set K is finite, fixed, and its feature vectors span R^d; the learner knows the arm/key-term bipartite graph W (key-term features)
The learner knows the conversation frequency function b(t)
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t=1,2,...,T$, a subset of arms $\mathcal{A}_t \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ are available to the agent to choose from. ... receives a corresponding reward $r_{a_t,t}\in[0,1]$. ... $r_{a_t,t}=\boldsymbol{x}_{a_t}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\theta}^*+\epsilon_t$, where $\epsilon_t$ is 1-sub-Gaussian random noise with zero mean. ... The key-term-level feedback on the key-term $k$ at $t$ is defined as $\tilde{r}_{k,t}=\tilde{\boldsymbol{x}}_{k}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\theta}^*+\tilde{\epsilon}_t$

settings.name_in_paper: Conversational contextual bandits (possibly time-varying key-term set)
unmapped: Conversational feedback: in addition to arm feedback, the learner may query up to floor(b(t)-b(t-1)) key-terms per round (b(t)=b*t) and observes noisy linear feedback x_tilde_k^T theta* + 1-sub-Gaussian noise for each queried key-term
The available key-term set K_t may vary over rounds; the learner knows the arm/key-term bipartite graph W (key-term features)
The learner knows the conversation frequency function b(t)
settings.definition_quote: ConLinUCB-MCR chooses a key-term as follow $k\in\mathop{\arg\max}\limits_{k \in \mathcal{K}_t}\alpha_t\norm{\boldsymbol{\tilde{x}}_{k}}_{\boldsymbol{M}_t^{-1}}$, where ... $\mathcal{K}_t\subseteq\mathcal{K}$ denotes the possibly time-varying key-terms set available at round $t$.

symbols.b_conv: conversation rate: b(t) = b*t key-term conversations up to round t, b in (0,1)
symbols.lambda_B: minimum eigenvalue of E_{k~unif(B)}[x_tilde_k x_tilde_k^T] for the barycentric spanner B of the key-term set

conditions: key-term feature vectors span R^d (barycentric spanner exists)
tuning: alpha_t = sqrt(2 log(1/delta) + d log(1 + (t+b(t))/(beta d))) + sqrt(beta)
key-terms sampled uniformly from a precomputed barycentric spanner

source.label: theorem1
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$ for some $\delta \in (0,\frac{1}{4}]$, the regret $R(T)$ of ConLinUCB-BS satisfies $R(T)\leq4\sqrt{\frac{2}{b\lambda_{\mathcal{B}}}}\sqrt{T}\Bigg(\sqrt{2\log(\frac{2}{\delta})+d\log(1+\frac{(1+b)T}{\beta d})}+\sqrt{\beta}\Bigg)+ \frac{256}{b\lambda_{\mathcal{B}}^2}\log(\frac{256d}{\lambda_{\mathcal{B}}^2\delta})+1$.

results.notes: Regret is defined via means against the per-round best available arm, bound holds w.h.p. The paper states this is O(d sqrt(T log T)) since lambda_B is O(1/d) (remark, not a formal statement). Paper's beta (regularizer) renamed beta_reg.

symbols.b_conv: conversation rate: b(t) = b*t, b in (0,1)

tuning: alpha_t = sqrt(2 log(1/delta) + d log(1 + (t+b(t))/(beta d))) + sqrt(beta)
key-term with maximal confidence radius selected

source.label: theorem4
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$ for some $\delta \in (0,1)$, the regret $R(T)$ of ConLinUCB-MCR satisfies $R(T)\leq2\sqrt{2Td\log(1+\frac{T+1}{\beta d})}\times\Bigg(\sqrt{\beta}+\sqrt{2\log(\frac{1}{\delta})+d\log(1+\frac{(b+1)T}{\beta d})}\Bigg)$.

results.notes: O(d sqrt(T) log T) order; does not exploit conversations in the rate. Applies to time-varying key-term sets.
